commentary:
Energy is the story this morning. Brent surged 3% to $94.39 and WTI jumped 3.3% to $88.67 after Ukraine struck Russia's Taneco refinery deep inland and a Black Sea oil terminal, deepening Moscow's second wave of gasoline shortages, while European TTF gas rallied 3.2% through €65/MWh for the first time since March — EU storage at just 62% keeping the winter supply premium alive. The oil bid put inflation risk squarely back on the radar and unravelled the bond rally sparked by Treasury Secretary Bessent's buyback surprise: 30-year Treasuries erased all their gains, the long bond fell 0.8%, and the curve bear-steepened as investors judged buybacks a short-lived fix for structurally higher term premium.

The macro backdrop reinforces the hawkish read. Fed minutes showed officials saw a need to hike if inflation doesn't cool, jobless claims printed a firmer-than-expected 206k, and softer big-box retail earnings — Walmart's miss knocked the consumer complex — muddied the growth picture without offering rate relief. That combination sank equity futures across the board: S&P -0.45%, Nasdaq -0.7%, with the Nikkei and KOSPI off 1.3% as rising global yields and energy-driven inflation feed on each other, a loop Japan's bond market is flagging first.

Transmission: stay wary of the long end — duration is the pressure point, not the front. Gold eased 0.75% and copper fell 1.2% on the firmer-yield, soft-China-demand mix, while grains caught a bid (corn and wheat +1%) on the energy pull-through. Watch refinery-strike escalation, EU storage builds, and whether yields force a deeper equity de-rating.
